fun_highlights: The vocation system genuinely differentiates lives at a structural level. A soldier's arc (a_soldier_service -> m_soldier_ghost -> e_soldier_old) produces a life that reads nothing like a scholar's (a_scholar_question -> m_scholar_legacy), and you can verify this in the transcripts: Carys Brandt's soldier life with PTSD flashbacks at age 56 and 'keep your head down' vs Iris Brandt's scholar life with the long-bet payoff and 'give it all away / guard it' are genuinely different shapes.

The callback system is the game's strongest mechanic. 'cb_lookaway' reaching back 46 years to the lonely child in the yard (Edmund Ashby, age 10 then 57), 'cb_books_late' closing the arc on the impossible childhood book (Ren Salvedi at 49 returning to the book from age 11), and 'cb_principle' making the adult pay a second price for a youthful stand — these land as earned moments. They are what the game does best.

The era system adds genuine macro-texture. Dynasty 6 House Salvedi opens on a war era, which gates the calling text differently ('There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young') and injects war-loss cards; Dynasty 15 House Lindholm opens lean years, bending the calling text and adding the 'share the last of it' card (Roman at 12, Joaquin at 16). This is visible, not just claimed.

Death as a shape rather than a punishment works. The early deaths — Anouk Ashby at 9 (Dynasty 10), Liv Quint at 31 (Dynasty 12), Soren Castellane at 18 (Dynasty 13) — are framed as complete and quiet rather than punitive. The collateral succession system (verified in dynasties that would otherwise end) keeps the dynastic arc alive without forcing every life into the child-bearing template.

The dynasty layer — mottos crystallizing from actual play ('Better a short blaze than a long smoke' for a reckless house, 'We give past what we can spare' for a generous one), heirlooms that gate callbacks (the book-too-hard, the soft-spot-for-strays triggering e_window), and the seat-gated cards (s_great_burden, s_patronage only for seat 4+) — gives the long session something to build toward that feels earned, not cosmetic.

The prose line pools are genuinely large. The observation system (engine.js `observe()`) for body-decline alone has 10 vit_tire variants and 9 vit_neg variants, and the child-birth pool has distinct late/early pools. Across 15 dynasties, exact phrase repetition in body-decline observations is rare — the texture does its job.
staleness: The childhood checklist is the most visible template in the transcripts. Across nearly every founder and heir: an early-world framing (c_origin), the book-on-the-desk (c_book), the fever (c_sick), the lonely child in the yard (c_friend), the sibling arrival (c_sibling), a move (c_move), and the wonder-moment (c_wonder) appear in clusters within the first 12 years with depressing regularity. In Dynasties 1-4, compare Carys Brandt age 4/9/16, Iris Brandt age 6/9/10/12/16, Henrik Brandt age 5/7/16, Greta Ashby age 5/10/16, Pavel Ashby age 8/14 — the same childhood beats land in nearly the same order. The engine's trait-affinity weighting (c_book for 'bookish', c_friend for 'warm') does some work, but not enough: most childhoods still hit 4-5 of the same 6-7 cards.

The calling fork is universal and the lines are thin. Every single life with a vocation receives the same 4-option fork — blade/book/hands/road — with the framing varying by era/seat but the choices identical. Then every scholar gets a_scholar_question and m_scholar_legacy; every maker gets a_maker_shop and m_maker_masterwork; every soldier gets a_soldier_service and m_soldier_ghost. This is the game's most mechanically legible seam: by generation 3 a player has seen every vocation arc at least once and the structure is fully exposed.

The 'love arrives / marriage / child' sequence runs on a nearly identical schedule across dynasties regardless of character. Looking at the transcripts: Carys age 46 love / age 50 child; Iris age 35 chosen-people / no marriage shown; Henrik age 24 love / age 30 married / age 42 child; Tobias age 25 love / age 40 married / age 34 child (reordered); Noor age 18 love / age 28 child / age 56 married. The engine's nudges (0.30 chance for y_love1, 0.55 for a_marry when late) cluster these events but do not produce genuinely different domestic shapes with high frequency. Most lives still have the love-marry-child arc; the solitary/childless lives feel like statistical accidents rather than designed alternate shapes.

The body-decline observation prose repeats structurally even when individual lines vary. Across the 15 dynasties, almost every life over 40 gets multiple body-decline observations from the same two pools (vit_tire, vit_neg). In a long session you stop reading them: 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them' / 'He has started to plan the day around what the body will permit' / 'Her body has become a small daily negotiation' — these fire reliably because the vitality decay is deterministic, and their cumulative effect across a dynasty session is to make every life feel like it slows down the same way. Dynasties 8, 9, 11, 14, 15 all feature 3+ consecutive body-observation lines in the elder years without a choice card interrupting.

The 'returning to the old town' callback (cb_left_home) fires in nearly every life that took the wanderer vocation or chose y_leave, which is a large fraction of lives. In the 15-dynasty transcript it appears in Carys (implied), Ronja, Anders Salvedi, Noor Ashby, Linnea Salvedi, Annika Okonkwo, Ottilie Quint, Joaquin Lindholm — always with the same framing of 'it shrank' or 'it was smaller than I remembered.' The two-choice structure (go back vs. let it stay a memory) and the outcome lines ('found it had shrunk to fit a smaller life than they now lived' / 'decided some places are better kept than seen') are overexposed. The card also triggers a *second* callback (cb_home_return in later content) which doubles the beat.

The epitaph pool has fewer truly distinct themes than the prose makes it look. 'Taught what they knew and so outlived the knowing of it' appears for Lazlo Bjornsen (Dynasty 5), Linnea Okonkwo (Dynasty 11, same words), and Junia Calloway gets a variant. 'Left people gentler than they found them' lands for Anders Salvedi (Dynasty 6) and Noor Ashby (Dynasty 8). The deduplication logic (RECENT_LINES, blocked()) works across adjacent lives in one dynasty but not cross-dynasty — so a player running many dynasties in one session hears the same epitaph clusters cycle back. The 'became_teacher' cluster dominates because the memory flag is earned by an unusually large number of paths.

improvements.what: Break the childhood checklist by assigning each child-stage card to a PRIMARY and SECONDARY trait pool that roughly halves which children see it. For example: c_wonder fires at high weight only for 'dreaming'/'bright' traits, c_friend fires at high weight only for 'warm'/'tender', c_dark fires primarily for 'guarded'/'frail', and c_steal fires primarily for children born into low-means households. Currently trait-affinity multiplies the weight by 2.6 (engine.js line 282) but all cards remain eligible for all children — raising the affinity to ~4.5 and tightening cond gates would mean a warm child gets c_friend + c_sibling but rarely c_dark, while a guarded frail child gets c_dark + c_sick but rarely c_wonder. The childhood template would diverge into 3-4 distinct early-life shapes rather than one checklist.
improvements.why: The childhood section is the most legible template in the transcripts and the first thing a returning player will notice. It accounts for roughly 6-8 cards of every life's opening that currently read as near-identical regardless of who the child is.

improvements.what: Add a fourth domestic shape: the 'deliberate solitary life' as a true arc, not a statistical fallback. Currently a childless/loveless life is mostly a life that missed the y_love1 nudge or where the player declined. There is no positive content for it until the elder phase (e_last_walk, cb_unspoken). Adding 3-4 adult cards gated on cond:()=>!rel('love')&&!rel('spouse')&&P.age>30 — moments about the particular texture of an unpartnered adult life (friendship as the primary bond, the particular freedom and cold of living alone, chosen family) — would make 'solitary life' a shape you can feel rather than an absence. Currently only Junia Calloway (Dynasty 7) has a life that genuinely reads as solitary, and even she marries at 56.
improvements.why: The engine already supports collateral succession so childless lives don't end dynasties, but the content for those lives is thin. Right now every solo life still pulls from the same romance cards (at reduced probability) rather than a distinct arc, so the life reads as a domestic arc that stalled rather than a different shape.

improvements.what: Give the 'cb_left_home' / hometown-return beat a richer branching resolution or add a cooldown that prevents it from firing in more than 1-in-3 lives. Currently it fires for any life that set left_home, which is a very common memory. Consider splitting it: a 'went back' path that can unlock a second beat (a person from the old life still living there, a specific consequence based on why they left), and a 'let it stay a memory' path that closes the arc differently for wanderers vs. those who left for the city. The current two-option structure produces the same outcome line ('it had shrunk to fit a smaller life') across too many lives.
improvements.why: This is the second-most-repeated single beat in the 15-dynasty transcript after the childhood checklist. It appears 7+ times and the prose variation is shallow.

improvements.what: Add a cross-dynasty epitaph suppression that runs longer than the current RECENT_CLUSTERS window of 14. The session-wide RECENT_LINES buffer (dynasty.js line 40) tracks verbatim lines but the cluster suppression (recentGC.slice(-9)) allows the 'teacher' or 'kind' cluster to recur every ~3 dynasties. Given a 15-dynasty session, this means the 'Taught what they knew, and so outlived the knowing of it' epitaph can appear 4-5 times. Expanding the cluster suppression to 15 entries (roughly the full session), and adding 3-4 new epitaph themes (the wanderer-life summary, the ruthless-but-effective life, the solitary-life-complete theme), would prevent the epitaph section from feeling like a short rotation.
improvements.why: Epitaphs are the single most visible line in a life's summary — they're the last thing you read before the heir screen. Verbatim repetition here breaks the illusion that each dynasty is genuinely different faster than anything else.

improvements.what: The vocation arc structure — 3 cards per calling, reliably seen in the same life-stages — would benefit from optional branch cards that only certain stat or memory combinations unlock within the arc. A soldier who chose 'keep your head down' at a_soldier_service and then refused to talk about it at m_soldier_ghost could face a different e_soldier_old: not 'what was it really like' but rather 'a young one knows you were a soldier and you have never said a word about it.' This would mean two soldiers who made different choices read differently in their elder years rather than both arriving at the same final card with a different answer.
improvements.why: The vocation arcs are the engine's best structural feature, but each arc is currently a 3-card sequence where variation comes only from which option you choose within each card, not from what sequence of cards you see. Adding 1-2 fork points inside each arc would substantially increase the space of possible soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer lives.

verdict: A Life has real strengths — the callback system, the vocation arcs, the era layer, and the dynasty accumulation all produce genuine variety across lives — but the childhood checklist and the domestic-arc template dominate a session heavily enough that the seams are visible by dynasty 3. The writing is often lovely, but the structure repeats: most lives open on the same 6 childhood cards in the same order, move through love-marry-child on a similar schedule, and close with body-decline observations and one of four or five elder reckonings. The score of 6.2 reflects a game that rewards a two- or three-dynasty session (the callbacks and dynasty layer haven't yet grown stale, and each vocation genuinely differs), but which degrades into template-recognition by a longer play session — exactly the staleness problem the genre's 'one more life' loop depends on resisting.
